description:
Found during the bedrock-61c.3 audit; pre-existing.

lib/bedrock/data_plane/log/shale/segment_recycler.ex, in `Server.handle_continue(:ensure_min_available, ...)`:

    {:error, reason} -> stop(reason, :shutdown)

`Bedrock.Internal.GenServer.Replies.stop/2` is `stop(state, reason) :: {:stop, reason, state}` (lib/bedrock/internal/gen_server/replies.ex:30). The arguments are reversed, so an allocation failure stops the recycler with reason `:shutdown` and installs the error atom as the GenServer's state.

## Failure scenario

The segment pool cannot allocate — ENOSPC on the log's filesystem, or EMFILE under fd pressure. The recycler exits with `:shutdown`, which reads as an orderly stop, and the actual cause (`:enospc`) is thrown away into the state field. The owning Shale log sees a benign-looking shutdown instead of a disk-full error, and the operator gets no signal identifying the real problem. `Shale.Server.classify_resource_error/1` exists precisely to distinguish `:enospc`/`:emfile`/`:enomem` — that classification is discarded here.

Note bedrock-61c.3 makes this path run more often: enforcing the pool ceiling means a later burst re-allocates rather than reusing retained segments, so `create_new_segments/2` is exercised on more workloads.

## Fix

`stop(:shutdown, reason)` — or better, pass the state and the classified reason explicitly. Audit other `stop/2` call sites for the same transposition.

## Test (write first, must fail)

Drive `handle_continue(:ensure_min_available, state)` with an unwritable path and assert the returned tuple is `{:stop, reason, state}` with the posix reason preserved and the state intact.
title: [BUG] SegmentRecycler handle_continue swaps stop/2 arguments, discarding the real failure reason
